name: Net-Zero Industry Act
evidence_rating: ex-ante only, no impact assessment: one think-tank critique; no measurement of the 40% benchmark
summary: The Act aims for EU factories to supply at least 40% of the EU's needs for clean technologies such as solar panels, batteries and heat pumps by 2030. It was proposed without an impact assessment, and economists at Bruegel called the 40% goal vague and protectionist. No study or official report has yet measured progress towards the goal or the Act's effect on investment.

indicators.objective: No formal impact assessment was prepared (urgency); the analysis was set out in staff working document SWD(2023) 68. The LFS gives no quantified indicators: the Commission will monitor via annual competitiveness reports on clean energy technologies and evaluate after three years

indicators.indicator: EU net-zero technology manufacturing capacity as share of annual EU deployment needs
indicators.target_or_baseline: At least 40% by 2030; 15% of world production by 2040
indicators.evidence: No published assessment of progress against the benchmark found; Bruegel criticised the 40% benchmark as poorly defined.
Commission to report annually; no figures verified.

indicators.indicator: Investment needed for EU net-zero manufacturing

literature.citation: European Commission (2023), Proposal for a Net-Zero Industry Act, explanatory memorandum, COM(2023) 161
literature.title: Proposal for a Net-Zero Industry Act, explanatory memorandum
literature.headline: Proposal not accompanied by an impact assessment owing to urgency; global market for key mass-manufactured net-zero technologies expected to reach about EUR 600bn a year by 2030 (IEA)
literature.summary_plain: The Commission proposed the Act without an impact assessment, pointing to a global clean-tech market worth about EUR 600 billion a year by 2030.

literature.citation: European Commission (2023), Investment needs assessment and funding availabilities to strengthen EU's Net-Zero technology manufacturing capacity, SWD(2023) 68
literature.title: Investment needs assessment and funding availabilities to strengthen EU's Net-Zero technology manufacturing capacity
literature.headline: Estimates EU investment needed in net-zero manufacturing; secondary reports put it at around EUR 92bn by 2030
literature.summary_plain: The Commission's background analysis estimated the investment needed to build EU clean-tech factories, reported at around EUR 92 billion by 2030.

literature.citation: Tagliapietra, Veugelers & Zettelmeyer (2023), Rebooting the European Union's Net Zero Industry Act, Bruegel Policy Brief 15/2023
literature.title: Rebooting the European Union's Net Zero Industry Act
literature.headline: Calls the proposal unconvincing: top-down technology picking, a poorly defined protectionist 40% self-sufficiency benchmark, reliance on permitting although it is not the main obstacle, ineffective procurement design and no governance structure
literature.summary_plain: Bruegel economists argued the Act picks technologies, sets a vague 40% self-sufficiency goal and targets permitting, which is not the main barrier to clean-tech investment.
